{{Short description|Infinite family of simple groups of Lie type}}
{{About| the infinite family of groups of Lie type found by Suzuki| the sporadic simple group | Suzuki sporadic group}}

In the area of modern algebra known as [[group theory]], the '''Suzuki groups''', denoted by  Sz(2<sup>2''n''+1</sup>), <sup>2</sup>''B''<sub>2</sub>(2<sup>2''n''+1</sup>), Suz(2<sup>2''n''+1</sup>), or  ''G''(2<sup>2''n''+1</sup>), form an infinite family of [[groups of Lie type]] found by {{harvs|txt|last=Suzuki|authorlink=Michio Suzuki (mathematician)|year=1960}}, that are simple for ''n'' ≥ 1. These simple groups are the only finite non-abelian ones with orders not divisible by 3.

==Constructions==

===Suzuki===

{{harvtxt|Suzuki|1960}} originally constructed the Suzuki groups as subgroups of SL<sub>4</sub>('''F'''<sub>2<sup>2''n''+1</sup></sub>) generated by certain explicit matrices.

===Ree===
Ree observed that the Suzuki groups were the fixed points of exceptional automorphisms of some [[symplectic group]]s of dimension 4, and used this to construct two further families of simple groups, called the [[Ree groups]]. In the lowest case the symplectic group ''B''<sub>2</sub>(2)≈''S''<sub>6</sub>; its [[Symmetric_group#Automorphism_group|exceptional automorphism]] fixes the subgroup Sz(2) or <sup>2</sup>''B''<sub>2</sub>(2), of order 20.
{{harvs|txt|last=Ono|year=1962}} gave a detailed exposition of Ree's observation.

===Tits===

{{harvs|txt|last=Tits|year=1962}} constructed the Suzuki groups as the symmetries of a certain ovoid in 3-dimensional [[projective space]] over a field of characteristic 2.

===[[Robert Arnott Wilson|Wilson]]===

{{harvs|txt|last=Wilson|year=2010}} constructed the Suzuki groups as the subgroup of the symplectic group in 4 dimensions preserving a certain product on pairs of orthogonal vectors.

==Properties==
Let ''q'' = 2<sup>2''n''+1</sup> and ''r'' = 2<sup>''n''</sup>, where ''n'' is a non-negative integer.

The Suzuki groups Sz(''q'') or <sup>2</sup>''B''<sub>2</sub>(''q'') are simple for ''n''≥1. The group Sz(2) is solvable and is the [[Frobenius group]] of order 20.

The Suzuki groups Sz(''q'') have orders ''q''<sup>2</sup>(''q''<sup>2</sup>+1)(''q''−1). These groups have orders divisible by 5, but not by 3.

The [[Schur multiplier]] is trivial for ''n''>1, [[Klein 4-group]] for ''n''=1, i. e. Sz(8).

The [[outer automorphism group]] is cyclic of order 2''n''+1, given by automorphisms of the field of order ''q''.

Suzuki group are [[Zassenhaus group]]s acting on sets of size (2<sup>2''n''+1</sup>)<sup>2</sup>+1, and have 4-dimensional representations over the field with 2<sup>2''n''+1</sup> elements.

Suzuki groups are [[CN-group]]s: the centralizer of every non-trivial element is [[nilpotent]].

===Subgroups===
When ''n'' is a positive integer, Sz(''q'') has at least 4 types of maximal subgroups.

The [[diagonal subgroup]] is cyclic, of order ''q'' – 1.

* The lower triangular (Borel) subgroup and its conjugates, of order ''q''<sup>2</sup>·(''q''-1). They are one-point stabilizers in a doubly transitive permutation representation of Sz(''q'').
* The dihedral group ''D''<sub>''q''–1</sub>, normalizer of the diagonal subgroup, and conjugates.
* ''C''<sub>''q''+2''r''+1</sub>:4
* ''C''<sub>''q''–2''r''+1</sub>:4
* Smaller Suzuki groups, when 2''n''+1 is composite.

Either ''q''+2''r''+1 or ''q''–2''r''+1 is divisible by 5, so that Sz(''q'') contains the Frobenius group ''C''<sub>5</sub>:4.

===Conjugacy classes===

{{harvs|txt|last=Suzuki|year=1960}} showed that the Suzuki group has ''q''+3 conjugacy classes. Of these, ''q''+1 are strongly real, and the other two are classes of elements of order 4.

*''q''<sup>2</sup>+1 Sylow 2-subgroups of order ''q''<sup>2</sup>, of index ''q''–1 in their normalizers. 1 class of elements of order 2, 2 classes of elements of order 4. 
*''q''<sup>2</sup>(''q''<sup>2</sup>+1)/2 cyclic subgroups of order ''q''–1, of index 2 in their normalizers. These account for (''q''–2)/2 conjugacy classes of non-trivial elements. 
*Cyclic subgroups of order ''q''+2''r''+1, of index 4 in their normalizers. These account for (''q''+2''r'')/4 conjugacy classes of non-trivial elements. 
*Cyclic subgroups of order ''q''–2''r''+1, of index 4 in their normalizers. These account for (''q''–2''r'')/4 conjugacy classes of non-trivial elements. 
The normalizers of all these subgroups are Frobenius groups.

===Characters===

{{harvtxt|Suzuki|1960}} showed that the Suzuki group has ''q''+3 irreducible representations over the complex numbers, 2 of which are complex and the rest of which are real. They are given as follows:

*The trivial character of degree 1.
*The [[Steinberg representation]] of degree ''q''<sup>2</sup>, coming from the doubly transitive permutation representation. 
*(''q''–2)/2 characters of degree ''q''<sup>2</sup>+1
*Two complex characters of degree ''r''(''q''–1) where ''r''=2<sup>''n''</sup>
*(''q''+2''r'')/4 characters of degree (''q''–2''r''+1)(''q''–1)
*(''q''–2''r'')/4 characters of degree (''q''+2''r''+1)(''q''–1).
